arcs: Portrait-procession (Lando, SOTY-verified): corner wordmark over full-bleed portrait -> pinned horizontal gallery -> on/off editorial split -> a discrete live 3D helmet gallery ('Helmets Hall of Fame') -> honours/partners -> inverted valediction close. One person told through facets over a Webflow DOM page; a 3D helmet feature (rotations + the gallery) recurs across facets — NOT a single scene tracked hero-to-footer (that stronger claim is unverified).

Rooms-procession / museum-after-hours (Cartier, winner-verified): scroll walks the visitor through six discrete staged 3D alcoves, one per artifact, transitioned by camera not by page; a persistent Web Audio score threads the rooms so the whole scroll is one narrated walk.

Single-object-dive (Oryzo, winner-verified): one subject held in the center of a live Three.js scene; scroll drives the camera through true Z-axis depth around and into it — the entire page is one continuous camera move on one object, never leaving it.

Location-flythrough (Primland, winner-verified): scroll = a continuous aerial camera gliding over real rendered terrain with atmospheric fog; the place unfolds beneath the reader as one uninterrupted move.

Playable-world (Messenger, Bruno Simon, winner-verified; Egg Hunt 2023 pre-window): the whole page is one operable 3D scene; a single clear verb (deliver / drive / dash-and-grab) is the narrative and the proof — the site is its own replay, there is no 'after the hero' because you never leave the scene.

Gated-reel (Siena, winner-verified): a costumed threshold gate (doubles as sound unlock) -> oversized-serif masthead over a scrubbed still -> operable filmstrip of treated stills -> per-work detail -> thin costumed credits; the shader canvas and grain run unbroken beneath.
story.thread: Winners pick ONE driven surface and never leave it — the single coaster object under a Z-diving camera (Oryzo, verified), the terrain the aerial camera glides over (Primland, verified), the persistent Mooders audio + camera through the six rooms (Cartier, verified), the tiny planet you pilot (Messenger, verified). The fil rouge is the medium itself, carried hero-to-footer by scroll (and, where earned, the pointer). Lando is the portrait-procession VARIANT — a 3D helmet feature recurring across DOM sections rather than one continuous in-engine scene — so its spine is softer (object-track over DOM, kept alive by Rive/canvas loops), not a never-leaving world. Cohesion is manufactured by three constants layered over the surface: one saturated accent that means 'active' on every element class (Lando lime #D2FF00, publicly corroborated; Siena red for the live state only), one named easing family (Siena --easeOutQuint cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1), CSS-verified; Lando's chrome bezier reported but not re-read this run), and one gesture grammar (inversion, or reveal-from-edge) that repeats while the per-class mechanic differs. The camera is the through-line: transitions between sections read as camera moves, never fades (Oryzo, Cartier, Primland).
story.copy: Sparse title-cards, never paragraphs — the medium carries the story, the words punctuate it. Person tracks subject: third-person for a personality (Lando), in-character for a world (Messenger). Label-length lines, one long declarative at most, idiomatic-warm verbs, an emphatic terminal period on a fragment, and a refusal to explain (no bullets, no hype, no exclamation). Quoted to calibrate specificity, never to ship: 'Always bringing the fight.' (a fragment with a full stop carries the close), 'Load Norris' (the wait put in-brand where a spinner would sit — and the archetype's designed load state), 'It's a small planet, but someone's gotta make the deliveries.' (the world's premise in one wry line). Imitate the specificity — the named place, the count, the refusal — never the wording.

spectacle_model.hero: The first viewport commits the DRIVEN MEDIUM: a real-time scene the visit moves through (Oryzo object, Cartier alcove, Hubtown monolith, Primland terrain), a scroll/pointer-scrubbed real sequence (Siena film still), or a full-bleed cinematic composed as the fold (Lando portrait + a live helmet feature). The commitment is legibility-in-one-beat AND aliveness-in-one-beat: the hero must read as one idea at a glance (Lando's driver-and-helmet is felt instantly) and it must already be driven — pointer-reactive or scroll-armed — because a pointer-dead, motion-dead WebGL hero is the archetype's first-impression defect (ERA's splash camera reacts to the cursor before a single scroll). The asset-heavy medium reaches the hero THROUGH a designed load state (see section_playbook 'load'), never a raw spinner. The scrubbed-sequence route carries the sequence-fidelity floor (imagery.md — Native resolution or nothing): every frame a distinct REAL sample (footage/render/drawn; corpus norm 30fps extraction, 89-1,182 frames per section) delivered at >= device pixels on the signature surface — the one 2x-upscaled winner ever measured (OPTIKKA, 1440px frames on retina) scored 7.3, the SOTD floor; synthetic in-betweens baked from a handful of stills have ZERO winner precedent. A live-animated full-resolution still (the Siena route) satisfies the FIDELITY floor only — it never satisfies this archetype's hero-medium verdict (dense and moving): on an immersive brief, stills-only material forces the re-scope conversation (failed footage-acquisition walk quoted + user confirmation, SKILL.md Phase 1), never a baked-down or single-still hero.
continuation: Lando: a 3D helmet feature recurs across the DOM page (rotations in the intro, a discrete 'Helmets Hall of Fame' gallery mid-page) rather than one continuously-tracked scene; pinned horizontal gallery (proof, ~7) -> on/off editorial split (the one rest beat, ~5) -> live 3D helmet gallery (mid PEAK, ~9) -> honours/partners with counter rolls (~6) -> valediction footer that returns the opening face helmeted (second PEAK, ~9). Rive + canvas ambient loops + ambient audio keep the page from freezing between inputs (exact instance counts and whole-scroll helmet tracking are unverified).

Oryzo: there is no 'after' — scroll is the spectacle. The camera moves through Z-depth on the one object every section; inertial physics easing keeps the object in motion between scroll ticks so it is never static. Amplitude peaks at the closest push-in; it never drops to silence.

Cartier: every section is peak-tier — scroll transitions the camera from alcove to alcove, each a fully staged 3D room; the Mooders Web Audio score plays unbroken as a narrative layer (not wallpaper); hidden gestures keep the pointer live throughout. There is no quiet section; the whole page is a sustained procession of staged moments.

Primland: the aerial camera glides continuously over terrain as you scroll — one uninterrupted flythrough; each scroll beat advances the camera and the narrative together, atmospheric fog and terrain always in motion.

ERA: chained WebGL scenes carry momentum — cursor-reactive splash camera -> interactive 3D map with particle traffic that animates on its own (living detail between inputs) -> parallax 'Road to Home' light path over a starfield -> camera zooms into architectural render detail on scroll. The scene is never a static backdrop.

Messenger / Bruno Simon: the continuation IS the whole page — one operable scene with ambient world life (other players, physics, drift); the visit sustains itself because there is nowhere to scroll to that leaves the medium.
evidence: Oryzo: the spectacle IS the continuous scroll-driven camera Z-dive on one object — no quiet section after the hero (Lusion BTS blog: vanilla Three.js, inertial physics, Z-axis camera).
Primland: one uninterrupted scroll-driven aerial flythrough over rendered terrain for the whole page — continuation is the mechanic, not an afterthought (Outpost case study).

Cartier: six sequentially staged 3D rooms, each at spectacle amplitude, threaded by an unbroken Mooders Web Audio score — sustained multi-peak, not one-peak-then-silence (utsubo teardown: scroll room-to-room).
Messenger / Bruno Simon: the whole page is one operable 3D scene — there is no 'after the hero' to fall quiet into (SOTD/SOTM-verified; Three.js + Cannon.js).

Lando (portrait-procession variant): the sectional multi-peak read still holds — a mid-page 3D helmet gallery + a palette-returning valediction over a Rive/canvas-animated DOM page; the 'never-idle 35 Rive/21 canvas' and 'whole-scroll tracking' legs are unverified and the thesis does NOT rest on them.

The archetype codifies the counter-law: a cinematic page that freezes between inputs breaks the fiction — silence after the hero is the defining defect, not restraint. The synthesis was independently confirmed against the verified in-engine winners this run.
spectacle_model.recommended_law: For the immersive archetype, replace 'exactly one climax' with the SPECTACLE-SPINE law: One continuous driven medium spans hero->footer — the spectacle spine, driven every section by scroll (camera Z-dive / room-to-room / flythrough / object-track) and, where earned, by pointer, and alive between inputs (ambient scene life + optional audio score). Within that spine, CAP the amplitude PEAKS at one or two (a mid-page maximal camera/physics/reveal moment, plus an optional inverted or returning close) — peaks are still scarce. The vocabulary of continuation is NOT capped: every section keeps the medium driven. The failure mode to forbid is the reverse of the other archetypes' over-peaking — here it is SILENCE: a section where the medium goes static or purely decorative (a stack of static images fading in with a particle canvas drifting behind) is 'aucune immersion', the defect. Peaks are capped; the spine is mandatory; a still section is the sin.

algorithm.decide: The story shape (arc), chosen by the subject — deterministic, one branch per subject type.
algorithm.rule: Single person/personality -> portrait-procession. Single object/product -> single-object-dive. A set of discrete artifacts -> rooms-procession. A physical place -> location-flythrough. A brand idea reducible to one verb -> playable-world. A treated archive/festival -> gated-reel. Pick exactly one; do not blend two arcs.

algorithm.decide: The signature thread (fil rouge) — the ONE driven surface and the three constants layered on it.
algorithm.rule: Name the single surface the narrative rides (the 3D object / scene / terrain / planet / helmet-over-DOM) and commit to never rendering it static — no section drops the medium to silence. Bind ONE accent that means 'active' on every element class, ONE easing family of 2-3 named beziers used everywhere, ONE gesture grammar (inversion, or reveal-from-edge). Cohesion lives in these constants; variety lives in the per-class mechanic. Never one hover everywhere; never a different ease per element.

algorithm.decide: The macrostructure — the ordered section chain that is the arc's beats.
algorithm.rule: Lay the sections as beats of the chosen arc (see section_playbook). The chain typically OPENS with a branded LOAD beat — the asset-heavy medium needs a designed first-load state (progress tied to real asset load), never a raw spinner (see section_playbook 'load'). Every subsequent section must keep the medium driven — a purely static/DOM-only section is illegal in this archetype (it is the silence defect). Rotate the section shapes against the previous stamp; never re-sequence a winner's ordering to taste.

algorithm.decide: The momentum map — the spine mechanic + the 1-2 capped peaks + the between-input life + long-scroll wayfinding.
algorithm.rule: Assign the SPINE: pick what scroll drives every section — camera Z-dive (single-object-dive), room-to-room camera transition (rooms-procession), aerial flythrough (location-flythrough), object-track over DOM (portrait-procession), or free-roam (playable-world). Place at most TWO amplitude PEAKS (a mid-page maximal camera/physics/reveal + an optional inverted/returning close). Fill BETWEEN inputs with named idle channels (ambient scene life: particle drift, physics settle, Rive/canvas loops, optional Web Audio score) so the page never freezes. For long scroll-jacked processions/flythroughs, EXPOSE wayfinding — a room/chapter index, scene counter, or progress rail bound to scroll or active-room index, keyboard- and skip-reachable — so the visitor can orient in the non-standard scroll (see gaps: procession-wayfinding). Verdict test: if any section's only motion is decorative over a static base, the spine was not built — fix before proceeding.

Cartier: spine = room-to-room camera + unbroken audio score; every room a peak (winner-verified)
ERA: idle life = self-animating particle traffic between inputs (case-study-verified)

algorithm.decide: Per-section pairing — the form and the interaction components for each role.
algorithm.rule: Pair each section role with its form + components from the section_playbook. Load -> branded-preloader (progress tied to real asset load, in-brand motif/copy; doubles as the sound-unlock gate when audio is used). Hero -> hero-masthead(media:back) or in-engine-hero or gated-splash, kinetic-reveal on h1, clip-reveal on media, shader-surface/webgl-scene ground. Continuation-spine -> dolly-zoom/scroll-camera-dive/rooms/flythrough. Proof/reel -> pinned-filmstrip, index-list+index-row-hover, full-bleed-figure procession, figure-hover. Rest -> editorial-split, char-assemble, text-emphasis-fill. Peak -> webgl-scene(delegated). Close -> valediction-footer (palette inversion) or contact-first close-panel.

algorithm.decide: Per-element interaction states — the differentiated hover/tap/focus per element class, DOM and in-scene.
algorithm.rule: Apply the element_states canon: CTA = full-token flood + label inversion (or already-solid motion-only), never a pale tint. Link = adopt-the-accent recolor. Figure = inner scale 1.1 in a clip frame + companion cue (or ellipse/edge-wipe uncover), never a 1.02-1.03 twitch. Index row = flood+invert or slide-to-expose-arrow with siblings dimmed 45-70%. Heading = variable-font axis animation only where a non-link display heading earns it; otherwise masked-line/char entrance, no generic hover. Nav = fixed/transparent/no-border/no-backdrop-filter, color transitions to stay legible. Cursor = OS default unless a mechanic earns a custom cursor that DRIVES the medium (camera or reveal). Interactive 3D MESHES answer the pointer via raycast: bounded highlight + pointer/grab affordance on hover, tap-to-act + a sub-160ms hit cue on touch, with a focusable DOM proxy for keyboard reach (element_states.scene_object). Run 4-5 distinct interaction channels (per-class states, display-type effect, cursor, idle, scroll texture); where the scene has interactive meshes, the in-scene raycast state is the channel that matters most for this archetype.
evidence: Lando: schedule rows flood lime + invert text; nav-link -> #B2C73A; helmet-grid img scale 1.1; text-nav-link wght/wdth axis (shipped-CSS specifics not re-read this run; standard-pattern mechanics kept as recipe)
Siena: all-work-cta flood #000/#fff .5s; review-he -> red; previousnext-item img 1.1; edge panel wipe (CSS-verified in an earlier run)
Messenger/Egg Hunt/Bruno: in-scene object taps + raycast interactions carry the playable-world verb (SOTD/SOTM-verified)

algorithm.rule: Pointer/cursor-camera classes go DORMANT on touch; scroll alone drives the scene (depth comes from scroll on mobile — the winner convention). Reconsider the WebGL scene, do not drop it: lower poly, fewer concurrent channels, progressive quality, budget under ~5MB init. Press-class elements answer the tap with a 90-160ms flash floor (the fill/press IS the tap answer); interactive scene meshes answer the tap via raycast-on-tap with a sub-160ms hit cue. Galleries -> native scroll-snap swipe + tap-to-enlarge. Cross-device parity is weighted highest here — judges check mobile first and a desktop-only WebGL hero tanks Usability (30%).
evidence: Messenger: 5.7MB init / 17.5MB max, responsive 8.4, animations 9.0 on mobile-capable Three.js (winner-verified scores)
reference: pointer-parallax/magnetic-cursor DORMANT on touch; swipe-snap-gallery is the scored Mobile Excellence line

Match the SPECIFICITY of the quoted winners (a named place, a count, a refusal), never the wording.

cta.hover: Full-token flood + label inversion: background jumps to a solid full-saturation token and text/icon flip to the contrast token (Lando .f1-highlight-grid:hover -> lime/black; Siena .all-work-cta-w:hover -> #000/#fff at .5s easeOutQuint). OR already-solid-at-rest CTA with motion-only hover (Lando .btn-w rests solid #D2FF00, press/scale only). NEVER a pale rgba(accent,.1) tint.
cta.tap: The flood/press IS the tap answer — a 90-160ms flash floor to the solid state on :active (pointer-dormant on touch, so the press must carry it).
cta.focus: Same as hover on :focus-visible (the flood + inversion), plus a visible focus ring — the hover-revealed state must be reachable by keyboard.

link.hover: Adopt-the-accent recolor — the link takes the site's one saturated accent otherwise reserved for the CTA (Lando nav-link -> #B2C73A, metadata -> lime; Siena .review-he -> red). Optional underline wipe or masked-label-swap for CTAs. Kinetic underline-draw is ABSENT in this tier (belongs to editorial) — body links use a bare text-decoration:underline.

figure.hover: Inner scale to 1.1 inside a fixed clip frame + a companion cue (scrim lift, tint, or caption rise) — Lando .helmet-grid-item:hover img, Siena .previousnext-item:hover .full-img-w. OR clip-path ellipse uncover ellipse(100% 120% at 50% 0%) (Lando visor motif), OR edge-anchored panel wipe scaleY(0->1) (Siena). Amplitude is 10%, never a dead 1.02-1.03.
figure.tap: Tap-to-enlarge (the scored Mobile Excellence line) or caption/meta reveal on tap; the static hairline/caption is the complete rest look.
figure.focus: Same as hover on :focus-within — hover-revealed caption/meta reachable under keyboard and touch.

index_row.hover: Hovered row lights (accent rule + surfaced metadata) while siblings dim to 45-70%. Mechanic differs per winner: flood the row + invert its text (Lando schedule rows lime + invert), OR hide the bullet and fade a direct-link in at .2s ease-out (Siena), OR slide the row text translate3d(1.3em,0,0) to expose the arrow (Lusion). :has() dims unhovered siblings.
index_row.tap: Row expands or navigates on tap; the surfaced metadata that hover reveals is present in the resting DOM (reachable under touch).
index_row.focus: Accent rule + surfaced meta on :focus-within, siblings dim — same spotlight, keyboard-driven.

heading.hover: Rare and only on a non-link display heading: variable-font axis animation — font-variation-settings 'wght'/'wdth' thicken and widen the letters in place (Lando .text-nav-link -> wght 660, wdth 93). This is the hero's one signature type move; it reads bespoke because almost nobody ships it. No generic hover on ordinary headings.
heading.tap: None (dormant on touch) — the entrance reveal is the mobile expression.
heading.focus: None as a hover analog; the accessible name stays clean via aria-label when chars/lines are split for the entrance (masked-line reveal or char-assemble on scroll-in).

nav.hover: Per-link: split-rollover (per-char stagger) or adopt-the-accent recolor. The bar itself: position:fixed, background:transparent, NO backdrop-filter, border-bottom:0 none — the text/icon color transitions (Lando color .75s cubic-bezier(.65,.05,0,1)) to stay legible over whatever section scrolls under it. Never a frosted panel on scroll, never a colored border-bottom.
nav.tap: Menu toggle answers the tap; link taps flash the accent.
nav.focus: Visible focus ring on links; nav reveals on scroll-up / hides on scroll-down and is keyboard-reachable when hidden.

cursor.hover: OS cursor by DEFAULT (the two deepest-evidence winners ship no cursor:none and no follower). An EARNED custom cursor must do real work on the medium: cursor-reactive camera giving dynamic scene angles (ERA), a mouse-reveal that uncovers geometry/lighting (Hubtown), or magnetic snap to [data-ad-magnetic] (Lando/Cuberto: speed .55, ease expo.out, stickDelta .15). The committed pointer layer lives here — a pointer-dead hero fails.
cursor.tap: Custom cursor and all pointer-camera/reveal classes go NATIVE/dormant on touch; the tap is answered by the press-class element or the scene-mesh raycast, not the cursor.
cursor.focus: N/A — cursor effects are pointer-only; keyboard users get the finished/revealed state without the pointer choreography.

scene_object.hover: Raycast highlight — on fine-pointer, the ray-hit interactive mesh answers with a bounded highlight (emissive lift, outline, or scale to ~1.05) and the cursor adopts a pointer/grab affordance signalling it is actionable (Cartier hidden gestures, Bruno project objects). Non-interactive meshes never highlight.
scene_object.tap: Tap-to-act with hit feedback — the tapped mesh performs its verb (dash, grab, open, drive-to) and answers with an immediate visual/haptic-class hit cue under 160ms; on touch the raycast fires on tap, not hover (Messenger object/emoji taps, Egg Hunt click-to-dash).
scene_object.focus: Interactive meshes are reachable via a focusable DOM proxy (a control or list) so the scene's actions are not pointer-only; focus mirrors the raycast highlight.

mobile_answer: Reconsider, don't downgrade. Pointer-driven classes (cursor-camera, mouse-reveal, magnetic, pointer-parallax) go DORMANT on touch and scroll alone drives the scene — on mobile the depth and the camera move come from scroll, the winner convention. The WebGL medium is reconsidered not dropped: lower poly, fewer concurrent channels, progressive quality low->high, budget under ~5MB init (Messenger ships 5.7MB init / 17.5MB max and still scores 8.4 responsive / 9.0 animations). Press-class controls answer the tap with a 90-160ms flash floor (the fill/press is the tap answer); interactive scene meshes answer the tap via raycast-on-tap with a sub-160ms hit cue. Galleries become native scroll-snap swipe tracks with tap-to-enlarge (the scored Mobile Excellence line). Cross-device parity is weighted higher in this archetype than any other — judges check mobile first and a desktop-only WebGL hero tanks the Usability score (30%) however impressive the canvas. prefers-reduced-motion swaps scrubbed media to a static poster and freezes the scene to a legible frame.

gaps.mechanic: A pinned WebGL section where scroll PROGRESS drives a real camera PATH through 3D depth — Oryzo moves the camera through true Z-axis depth around/into one object; Primland glides an aerial camera over rendered terrain; ERA zooms the camera into architectural render detail on scroll. Spec: bind ScrollTrigger scrub to a camera-path timeline (position + lookAt keyframes, optional FOV), reversible, driven inside the render loop (no per-frame layout/paint); inertial easing so the subject stays in motion between scroll ticks; optional fade/dissolve hand-off at the end of the travel; degrades to a static hero frame under reduced-motion and on touch scroll-only. dolly-zoom in the manifest is the 2.5D cousin (a media element scaling toward a focal point) — this is the true-3D camera-through-a-scene spine mechanic the momentum model needs and the recipes cannot execute today.

A macrostructure/recipe where each section is a DISCRETE staged 3D scene and scroll transitions the CAMERA (cut or dissolve) from one to the next — Cartier's six self-contained alcoves 'like rooms in a museum after hours', one per artifact; a persistent audio + ambient life threads the rooms. Spec: an ordered array of staged scenes sharing one canvas + one camera rig; scroll drives inter-room transitions (camera move or curtain-transition); each room owns its lighting/composition; distinct from engine-world (single continuous scene) and portrait-procession (DOM sections over one static-framed canvas). The 'succession of staged 3D moments' arc has no recipe today.

A first-load screen designed as a signature beat, not a spinner — progress is tied to REAL asset loading (Three.js LoadingManager / preloaded texture + model bytes), carrying an in-brand motif or copy where a spinner would sit (Lando puts the wait in-brand: 'Load Norris'). Spec: gate the scene reveal on a progress value derived from actual load events (0->1), animate a branded progress indicator, hand off to the hero with a camera/reveal transition (not a hard cut); when audio is used the loader doubles as the sound-unlock gate (autoplay policy). The archetype is the most asset-heavy of all, so the load state is the first impression — the playbook quotes 'Load Norris' in copy but encoded no loader role until this revision. degrades to a static poster under reduced-motion.

Per-object interaction states for discrete interactive meshes INSIDE the 3D scene — the hover/tap axis the DOM element canon omits. Spec: a raycaster maps pointer/tap to scene meshes; on fine-pointer hover of an interactive mesh, apply a bounded highlight (emissive lift / outline / scale ~1.05) and switch the cursor to a pointer/grab affordance; on tap/click, run the mesh's verb (grab / open / drive-to / dash) with an immediate sub-160ms hit cue; non-interactive meshes never respond; on touch the raycast fires on tap (no hover). Provide a focusable DOM proxy so scene actions are keyboard-reachable. element_states covers DOM classes (cta/link/figure/index_row/heading/nav) + a camera/reveal cursor but nothing for the in-scene mesh — the one hover surface most central to this archetype (now added as element_states.scene_object).

Fine-pointer DRIVES the WebGL hero — Hubtown's cursor uncovers detail in the geometry and lighting (a reveal mask / light bound to pointer position); ERA's splash camera reacts to cursor movement giving dynamic angles. Spec: on fine-pointer, lerp a scene parameter to pointer position — either a reveal mask/spotlight over the scene, or a camera orbit/parallax offset (bounded, ~differential lerp 0.1); DORMANT on touch (scene runs on scroll alone). The manifest has pointer-parallax (DOM-layer depth) and magnetic-cursor (element snap) but NOTHING that drives the 3D medium with the pointer — this is the committed-pointer-layer law made executable for the WebGL hero.

A gated ambient audio bed treated as a NARRATIVE LAYER, not wallpaper — Cartier's bespoke Mooders soundscape plays through the whole experience via Web Audio API. Spec: the arrival gate (gated-splash / enter control) doubles as the sound-unlock (browser autoplay policy blocks unmuted audio); a persistent mute toggle; WebM/Opus first with MP3 fallback; ambient bed at 0.05-0.15 volume, micro-interaction stings under 0.3s; pause on visibilitychange; silent under prefers-reduced-motion. The reference names Howler.js and mandates a sound gate but ships no component; this is the missing sensory channel that sustains momentum between visual inputs.

Orientation for a long scroll-jacked procession or flythrough — the spectacle-spine mandates a long driven scroll but gives it no wayfinding, and nav is specced as a fixed transparent bar only. Spec: a room/chapter index, scene counter, or progress rail bound to scroll progress (or the active room/beat index), showing where the visitor is in the non-standard scroll and offering skip/jump targets; keyboard- and skip-link-reachable. Distinct from the fixed transparent nav (top-level chrome). Evidence is inferential from Cartier's discrete six-room architecture and Primland's beat structure rather than a single cited component (MEDIUM).

One clear VERB the visitor performs inside the WebGL scene, replayable, no tutorial/no menu — deliver mail on a tiny planet (Messenger), click-to-dash and grab eggs (Egg Hunt), drive a car through a town (Bruno), aim/time a shot (Lacoste). Spec: a delegated one-verb loop with instant readability, optional score/high-score chase, the site-IS-the-replay close; inherently bespoke (delegated to a WebGL path) but worth a recipe slot so the composer knows the playable-world arc exists and how it collapses all funnel jobs into one operable scene. Lower priority because it is inherently hand-built, not a drop-in.
gaps.status: merged-as-composition(recipe order routed to closure pass)

gaps.mechanic: Self-animating detail INSIDE the WebGL scene that keeps it alive between inputs — ERA's particle-object cars following road paths, Jordan Breton's butterflies/wind/waterfall, Messenger's other players drifting. Spec: instanced/particle ambient motion within the scene (traffic, drift, flora), IO- and visibilitychange-gated, compositor-cheap. Related to the DOM-level ambient-idle component but lives in-canvas — the between-input life that makes the spine never freeze. Priority 3 because it is scene-specific and rides the delegated WebGL path.

variation: This section_playbook is one legal costume of the archetype, never THE skeleton. Structure is story-native (SKILL.md Phase 1): the body's sections derive from the universe's spine, then check against these roles for coverage — never the reverse. The axes serial winners measurably rotate between builds (21-artifact corpus, 5 studios): body content archetype + item counts, the ONE signature device (never reused across builds), the close mechanism, the hero medium, the index/HUD costume. What persists as DNA: type grammar, motion register + interaction vocabulary, annotation grammar as a form, engineering architecture. The same content archetype + item count + close mechanism recurring across two different-brand builds has zero winner precedent.
